  VII.    THE PROFIT DISTRIBUTION PROPOSAL OR PROPOSAL ON TRANSFER OF CAPITAL RESERVE FUND INTO
          SHARE CAPITAL FOR THE REPORTING PERIOD CONSIDERED AND APPROVED BY THE BOARD

  The Company proposes to distribute cash dividends to the Shareholders based on the total number of Shares
  determined on the record date fixed for the equity distribution which will be specified in the equity distribution
  implementation announcement. The Company proposes to distribute cash dividends of RMB6.80 (tax inclusive) for
  every ten Shares, i.e. RMB0.68 (tax inclusive) for each share held by Shareholders, totaling RMB923,211,868.16
  (tax inclusive) based on the total share capital of the Company of 1,357,948,412 (including 868,907,512 A
  Shares and 489,040,900 H Shares) as at 28 February 2026, and deducting the 283,900 H Shares repurchased
  pending cancellation, being 1,357,664,512 Shares (including 868,907,512 A Shares and 488,757,000 H Shares).
  Total cash dividend of the Company for 2025 (including 2025 interim cash dividend already paid) amounted to
  RMB1,520,709,169.44 (tax inclusive). The 2025 dividend of the Company accounted for approximately 37.12% of
  the net profit attributable to Shareholders of the Company as contained in the consolidated financial statements
  for 2025. In case of any change in the total share capital of the Company from the date of the profit distribution
  announcement to the record date for implementation of the equity distribution, the Company proposes to maintain
  the payout amount per Share unchanged, make corresponding adjustments to the total payout amount, and will
  publish separate announcement(s) on the specific adjustments. The above profit distribution plan has been considered
  and approved at the 24th meeting of the seventh session of the Board, and is subject to consideration and approval
  at the 2025 annual general meeting of the Company.

CHAIRMAN’S
STATEMENT
    Chairman’s Statement




          Dear Investors,

          Best greetings!

          On behalf of the Board of Directors, I hereby present to you the
          2025 annual report of the Company, and would like to extend my
          sincere gratitude to all our partners for their long-term support
          and concern about our development.




    The year of 2025 marked the final year of the “14th Five-Year” Plan period as well as the 20th anniversary
    of Times Electric. Throughout the year, Times Electric forged ahead with fortitude and determination. We
    earnestly implemented national strategies and the management requirements of the Board, stayed committed to
    innovation-driven development, and overcame various difficulties amid fierce market competition to achieve steady
    progress. With the sound decision-making of the Board and the concerted efforts of all employees, the Company
    stayed focused on both the transportation and energy sectors, and pursued high-quality development as its core
    theme. The Company achieved another record high in operating performance, successfully delivering a satisfactory
    closing performance for the “14th Five-Year” Plan period.


    (I)       Adhering to the coordinated advancement of businesses and achieving parallel development across the six
              segments. Based on the dual strategic tracks of transportation and energy, the Company adhered to concentric
              diversification with concerted efforts, deepened collaborative growth, and significantly improved operational
              quality and efficiency. The rail transit sector served as the cornerstone for stability, with the market share of
              traction systems maintaining a leading position, and the industrial standing of power supply, signaling, door
              systems and other businesses steadily enhanced. Semiconductors, automotive equipment, new energy power
              generation, marine equipment, industrial equipment and other strategic emerging sectors gathered momentum
              for breakthroughs and achieved simultaneous improvement in both scale and quality. The construction of the
              factory building and the installation of the first-phase equipment for the Zhuzhou Phase III semiconductor
              project were completed, realising smooth tape-out and production. The Indonesia base of CRRC Electric Drive
              was completed and put into operation, marking the first step in the Company’s overseas layout.




10 ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD. 2025 Annual Report
                                                         Chairman’s Statement
(II)    Adhering to the guidance of scientific and technological innovation, and significantly strengthening technical
        strength. The Company deeply integrated scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation,
        and comprehensively consolidated its leading technological edge. It established a full-operating-condition
        high-fault-tolerance system for permanent magnet traction systems, developed 400kW+ PV inverters using
        hybrid SiC three-level topology, finished the R&D of the fifth-generation pure electric high-voltage SiC
        all-in-one electric drive platform, and achieved breakthroughs in fourth-generation trench-gate SiC MOSFET
        chips, ETCS multi-system integrated switching and other technologies. The six industrial segments maintained
        their leading technological positions.


(III)   Adhering to refined management for quality improvement and fully embracing the intelligent transformation.
        The Company continuously deepened the application of digital and intelligent technologies, providing solid
        support for higher quality and efficiency in industrial operations. It fully promoted the operation cockpit,
        establishing a transparent, efficient and coordinated decision-making and command system. It deepened the
        data integration of the LTC process, achieving steady progress in capital collection efficiency. The restructuring
        of the core ITR process delivered prominent effects and enhanced the efficiency of on-site fault data collection.
        The Company promoted the QMS quality management system, consolidating the quality control foundation of
        all subsidiaries. It established a new collaborative paradigm for treasury, business and finance, driving the deep
        integration of fund management and business operations. Eleven AI application scenarios were implemented,
        ushering in a new stage of intelligent business development.


(IV)    Adhering to reform for empowered development and steadily strengthening core competencies. The Company
        acted in strict accordance with the “Three Inspirations, Three Efficiencies, and Three Capabilities” requirements
        of CRRC Group, and advanced corporate reforms in a thorough and pragmatic manner. It was once again
        awarded the highest “Benchmark” rating among “Science Reform Enterprises” by the State-owned Assets
        Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) of the State Council, and retained the top benchmark title
        among CRRC Group’s “Science Reform Enterprises”. Times Electric Semiconductor completed the joint-stock
        system reform; CRRC Electric Drive made substantial progress in the pilot program for the empowerment of
        scientific and technological achievements, and was selected as a “Qihang Enterprise” by SASAC.


We sail forward with momentum at this promising time, and draw a grand blueprint to open a new chapter. Building
on a new historical starting point and embarking on a new journey of development, Times Electric will continue
to align closely with national development strategies, fully implement the major strategies of building “a strong
transportation country”, “a strong marine country”, and “a strong manufacturing country”, and fully leverage the
three key roles of state-owned enterprises in technological innovation, industrial control, and security support. We
will continuously enhance our core competitiveness and core functions, fully release the synergy of the six industrial
sectors, and strive to compose a new chapter of high-quality development during the “15th Five-Year” Plan period.


The year of 2026 marks the inaugural year of the “15th Five-Year” Plan. We will stay unwaveringly committed to the
central task of pursuing high-quality development, adhering to the guiding principles of Party building leadership,
reform-driven empowerment, innovation-led growth, quality first, and intelligent transformation. We will further
explore new scenarios and markets for our advantageous industries, focus on enhancing profitability in our growing
industries, and continue building a “Times Electric of Four Higher Standards”.




Li Donglin
Chairman
Zhuzhou, Hunan, the PRC
27 March 2026

    interest and taxes, fully reflect the operational ability and profitability of the Company’s core business, and reflect the

    I.     THE COMPANY’S PRINCIPAL BUSINESS, OPERATING MODELS, AND INDUSTRY
           LANDSCAPE DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
    (I)    Principal Business and Major Products or Services
    As a pioneer and leader in China’s electrified railway equipment industry, the Company has carried the mission and
    responsibility of revitalising the high-end equipment sector for over 60 years. Dedicated to the independent R&D
    and industrialisation of traction drive and control systems, widely recognised as the “heart” and “brain” of trains, it
    continues to lead the domestic market for rail transit electrical systems.


    The Company is mainly engaged in the R&D, design, manufacturing and sales of rail transit equipment products and
    the provision of related services, and has an industrial structure of “components + systems + complete machines”.
    Its products mainly include rail transit electrical equipment (primarily traction converter systems of rail transit
    vehicles), railway engineering machinery and communication signal systems. Meanwhile, the Company actively
    expands to industries other than rail transit, and conducts business in the fields of semiconductors, automobile, new
    energy, marine and industrial operations. After years of R&D efforts and technology accumulation, the Company
    has developed a completely independent intellectual property right system, and has become a high-tech enterprise
    with independent intellectual property rights in the fields of electrical system technology, converter and control
    technology, industrial converter technology, train control and diagnosis technology, railway engineering machinery
    technology, power semiconductor technology, communication signal technology, data and intelligent application
    technology, traction power supply technology, inspection and testing technology, deep-sea robotic technology, new
    energy vehicle electric drive system technology, and sensor technology.


    Since its establishment, the Company’s principal business has not changed significantly.


    Information about significant new non-core businesses
    □Applicable    ✔ Not applicable


    (II)   Major Operating Models
    In terms of procurement mode, the Company adopts the model of “unified management, professional centralised
    management and separation of procurement duties”, establishes a unified set of measures, methods and procedures
    for procurement, performs centralised procurement and promotes a unified procurement platform, so as to ensure
    procurement quality, reduce costs and increase efficiency.


    In terms of production model, the Company adopts the planning management model of determining production by
    sales. Under this model, the Company formulates sales plans according to sales orders and previous sales results,
    maintains a safety inventory based on daily demand assessment and coordination of production, supply and sales,
    and then determines the production plan. Based on the principle of “lean, efficient and dynamic management and
    comprehensive balance”, the Company has built an integrated, flexible, efficient and intelligent production planning
    system suitable for its development.




22 ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD. 2025 Annual Report
                                                    Report of the Directors
In terms of service model, the Company has established a global after-sales service network covering key customers,
key regions and key products. With a three-level service management model underpinned by “service headquarters,
service areas, and service stations”, coupled with a three-tier technical support system consisting of “R&D technology
– headquarters technology – field technology”, the Company promptly responds to customer needs and ensures that
customers can obtain after-sales services, technical support, quality feedback and complaint consultation at any time.


In terms of sales model, the Company obtains orders through market-oriented public bidding, competitive
negotiation, single-source procurement by customers, and customer inquiry, and produces and sells products
according to customer needs. Currently, the Company mainly adopts the direct sales model to sell products.


In terms of R&D model, the Company adheres to a “strategy-driven” and “market-oriented” approach (two-wheel
drive), and determines research projects and carries out scientific research work from the perspectives of strategy and
market. By introducing the concept of IPD and project triangle, the Company extends technology innovation to market
research and product planning and to the life cycle management of mass-produced products, thus realising the whole
process management of products from strategic planning, scientific research and development to commercialisation.


(III)   Industry Landscape
1.      Development stage, basic characteristics, and main technical barriers of the industry
The Company is mainly engaged in the R&D, design, manufacturing and sales of rail transit equipment products
and the provision of related services. According to the National Economic Industry Classification (GB/T4754-2017)
of the National Bureau of Statistics, the Company belongs to the “C37 railway, shipbuilding, aerospace and other
transportation equipment manufacturing industry”; according to the Classification of Strategic Emerging Industries
(2018) (NBS Order No. 23) issued by the National Bureau of Statistics, the Company belongs to the “2.4 Rail transit
equipment industry of 2. High-end equipment manufacturing industry”. The Company’s rail transit equipment mainly
includes rail transit electrical equipment, rail engineering machinery and communication signal systems, which belong
to the respective sub-sectors under “2.4 Rail transit equipment industry of 2. High-end equipment manufacturing
industry” as set out in the Classification of Strategic Emerging Industries (2018).


The Company’s emerging equipment products are primarily applied in semiconductor, automobile, new energy,
marine and industrial fields, some of which are used in the field of rail transit.


In the rail transit equipment industry which is characterised by high core technology barriers, customers have very
high requirements for safety, reliability and sustainability of products and services provided, and enterprises need to
have strong anti-risk capabilities. Driven by core technologies, the Company will continue to innovate and develop
smarter and greener high-end equipment based on such application scenarios as railways, urban rail transit, new
energy vehicles, new energy power generation, deep-sea equipment, mining, ports, metallurgy and vessels. After
years of accumulation, the Company’s self-developed core technologies and multidisciplinary professional capabilities
spanning from components to complete machines represent the main barriers for the rail transit industry and
high-end industrial equipment industry.

    2.     Analysis of the Company’s industry position and its changes
    In the rail transit sector, the Company is a leading supplier of traction converter systems in China’s rail transit industry,
    capable of producing systems covering a wide range of vehicle types, including high-speed trains, locomotives, and
    urban rail vehicles. The Company’s traction converter systems feature a comprehensive product portfolio and hold
    a dominant market share. Its traction converter systems for high-speed railways and locomotives are widely applied
    in core vehicle models such as the Fuxing and Hexie series, consistently leading the domestic market for many years.
    According to public information such as market bidding statistics, the Company’s urban rail traction converter system
    has ranked first in domestic market share for fourteen consecutive years, from 2012 to 2025. Baoji CRRC Times, a
    subsidiary of the Company, is one of the three manufacturers of road maintenance machinery designated by State
    Railway Group. With about 73 administrative licenses, it can produce more than 50 kinds of products in multiple
    series, including heavy-duty railway vehicles, catenary vehicles, large road maintenance machinery, and urban rail
    transit engineering vehicles, and continuously expands to the passenger line and urban rail markets.


    Driven by technological R&D as its core competency, the Company adheres to a “concentric diversification” strategy.
    While consolidating and advancing its rail transit equipment business, it actively expands into emerging equipment
    sectors beyond rail transit to create new growth drivers. In the semiconductor field, the Company began its R&D
    and industrialisation of power semiconductor technology in 1964. Through sustained investment and platform
    upgrades, it has emerged as a representative IDM player mastering technologies in high-power thyristors, IGBTs,
    IGCTs, SiC devices, and their corresponding modules. It boasts a complete industrial chain encompassing chips,
    modules, devices, and systems, and has established industrialisation bases for 6-inch bipolar devices, 8-inch IGBTs,
    and 8-inch SiC devices. The Company’s full series of high-reliability IGBT products has broken the monopoly of
    foreign enterprises in core components for rail transit and UHV transmission. It holds a leading domestic market share
    in high-power modules for rail transit and smart grids. In the automotive sector, according to NE Times, its power
    modules for passenger vehicles ranked second in the industry by installed capacity in 2025, capturing a 13.8% market
    share. In the new energy sector, the Company’s products include photovoltaic inverters, energy storage converters,
    wind power converters, and IGBT hydrogen production power supplies. It is actively building a presence within the
    “wind-solar-storage-hydrogen” ecosystem, primarily centered around key state-owned enterprise groups including
    the “Big Five and Six Small” power groups, the “Two Grids and Two Construction” corporations, and the “Three
    Oil and Gas” giants. The Company has achieved sustained growth in both market share and new contracts signed
    for photovoltaic inverters, with annual bids approximating 18GW, ranking among the top in the domestic industry.
    Its wind and energy storage converter business is progressing rapidly, actively expanding its customer base. The
    IGBT hydrogen production power supply maintains a leading edge, holding the largest market share in China. In the
    automotive field, as the only central enterprise in the electric drive system sector, the Company possesses a complete
    industrial chain capability encompassing “key devices – core components – system integration”. According to NE
    Times, its annual installed capacity of range-extender systems for new energy vehicles ranks among the top in the
    domestic market. Its sensing devices firmly hold the largest domestic market share in the rail transit sector and power
    sensors are also among the industry leaders in the new energy vehicle, wind power, and photovoltaic sectors. In the
    marine field, the Company entered the “deep blue” sector in 2015 by acquiring SMD Ltd., the world’s second-largest
    designer and manufacturer of deep-sea robotics. This move filled a gap in China’s domestic deep-sea robotics
    industry. Products such as underwater trenching robots and remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) now account for half
    of the global market in the field of self-propelled underwater trenching and cable laying engineering machinery. In
    the industrial field, the Company holds a leading position in niche areas such as electric drives for mining trucks, air
    conditioner inverters, and metal rolling mills.


    The Company will constantly improve user experience and strengthen differentiated competitive advantages based
    on customer needs. Through continuous innovation in business, technology and management, the Company seeks to
    provide intelligent, safe, green and comfortable high-end equipment for the society, and become a preferred supplier
    of integrated electrical system solutions in the transportation and energy fields.

From an international perspective, the once-in-a-century global transformation is unfolding at an accelerated pace,
and a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing deeply.
Geopolitical competition across the globe has intensified, unilateralism and trade barriers are on the rise, and the
external environment has become significantly more unstable and uncertain. Amid such shifts, the Belt and Road
Initiative and regional cooperation mechanisms such as RCEP continue to deepen, providing a new platform for
Chinese enterprises to “go global” and opening up critical strategic opportunities for the Company to further expand
its international presence in the rail transit and new energy sectors.


From a domestic perspective, the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee explicitly called for
“accelerating the development of new productive forces” and “building a new type of whole-nation system”,
providing clear guidance for industrial upgrading and the development of a modern industrial system. The nation has
fully implemented the strategy of expanding domestic demand and fostered a new development pattern of “dual
circulation”, while continuously strengthening policy support for strategic emerging industries, the digital economy,
green and low-carbon development, and smart manufacturing. This has provided solid policy support and broad
development space for the Company to sustain investment and further strengthen its core sectors, including rail
transit equipment, new energy equipment and power semiconductors.


Global economic growth momentum has weakened, the international economic and trade order has been disrupted,
external demand recovery remains sluggish, and instability and vulnerability have become increasingly prominent.
Nevertheless, China’s economy boasts strong resilience, great potential and ample vitality, and its long-term positive
fundamentals remain unchanged. The Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee stressed the need
to “sustain the upward momentum of economic recovery”. By adopting a package of policies including expanding
effective investment, promoting industrial structure upgrading, deepening the energy revolution and strengthening
scientific and technological supply, the state has injected strong new impetus into high-end equipment, green
industries and smart manufacturing.


China’s ultra-large market advantage, complete industrial system, growing innovation capacity and abundant
talent dividend have created favorable conditions for the Company to expand its market share and enhance the
security level of the industrial chain in strategic sectors including rail transit, new energy and power semiconductors.
Meanwhile, amid the energy revolution, the development of a new-type power system and the restructuring of the
global industrial chain, the industries in which the Company operates will maintain a medium-to-long-term growth
trend, laying a solid economic foundation for the Company’s high-quality development.


At present, the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is accelerating.
Digitalisation, intelligentisation and greening have become the main themes of industrial upgrading. The deep
integration of artificial intelligence, big data, cloud computing, 5G/6G with power semiconductors and new energy
technologies is reshaping the technological foundation and competitive landscape of the equipment manufacturing
industry. The Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee emphasised “driving industrial innovation
through scientific and technological innovation” and “breaking through key core technologies”, which has charted
the strategic course for the Company to enhance its capacity for self-reliance and self-improvement in science and
technology in such fields as power semiconductors, new energy equipment, intelligent traction and control, AI
manufacturing and digital twins.

    II.    DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF OPERATIONS
    China’s railway construction achieved remarkable results in 2025. According to data released by China State Railway
    Group, China’s railway fixed-asset investment reached RMB901.5 billion in 2025, representing a year-on-year
    increase of 5.98% and hitting a new record high. By the end of 2025, the national railway operating length stood at
    165,000 kilometers, including 50,400 kilometers of high-speed railways. Urban rail transit construction maintained
    steady development. According to statistics from the China Urban Rail Transit Association, by the end of 2025, a
    total of 382 urban rail transit lines had been put into operation in 58 cities nationwide, with an operating length of
    13,071.58 kilometers. Guided by the goals of peaking carbon emissions by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by
    2060, China’s new energy industry has accelerated its development. In particular, data from the China Association of
    Automobile Manufacturers showed that in 2025, the production and sales of new energy vehicles in China reached
    16.626 million units and 16.49 million units respectively, up 29% and 28.2% year on year. China ranked first in the
    world for 11 consecutive years. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles further rose to 52.3% in December and
    47.9% for the whole year. Data from the National Energy Administration showed that China’s total installed power
    generation capacity reached 3.89 billion kilowatts by the end of 2025, representing a year-on-year increase of 16.1%,
    including 1.20 billion kilowatts of solar power installed capacity, up 35.4% year on year, and 640 million kilowatts
    of wind power installed capacity, up 22.9% year on year. Adhering to high-quality development as its core guideline,
    the Company has prioritised the enhancement of profitability as the central objective of its annual operation and
    management. With dedication and enterprise, all employees have united to effectively respond to external challenges,
    while continuously optimising its business layout and promoting the balanced and phased development of its six
    industrial sectors, advancing the construction of a “CRRC with Four Higher Standards”. In 2025, the Company
    achieved steady growth in operating performance and continuous improvement in key indicators, delivering a solid
    and remarkable annual performance.


    (I)    Breakthroughs in Rail Transit Business
    Taking advantage of the growth in railway investment by China State Railway Group, the Company continued to
    deliver EMUs and locomotives, maintaining a stable market position. It helped the CR450 EMU prototype achieve
    a cumulative fault-free operation of over 360,000 kilometers, setting a new record of a single-train speed of
    453 km/h and a relative meeting speed of 896 km/h. The Company conquered the complete set of technologies
    for the flexible through-phase power supply system, completed China’s first demonstration project of the
    “grid-source-storage-vehicle” coordinated energy supply system for heavy-haul railways, and realised the first
    commercial application of permanent magnet traction technology in China’s high-power new energy locomotive field,
    providing a brand-new solution for the green and low-carbon transformation of heavy-haul transportation scenarios.
    According to statistics from RT Rail Transit Network, the Company’s domestic market share of urban rail traction
    systems was 60.92% in 2025, leading the industry for 14 consecutive years. Maintenance revenue maintained steady
    growth; in overseas business, the Company won multiple projects in Asia, the Americas and other regions. In terms
    of rail engineering machinery, the first batch of rail engineering vehicles meeting European standards was officially
    delivered. The communication and signaling business made steady progress: Ningbo Line 8 was put into operation in
    June, marking the landing of the first independent FAO application demonstration project; Hefei Line 6 was put into
    trial operation in December, further verifying the Company’s professional capabilities as a systematic solution provider
    for the seamless split transformation and integration of fully independent FAO. In addition, the power supply system
    won Chongqing Line 27, China’s first general contracting project for power supply system engineering, and the
    platform door business ranked among the top 3 domestically in the industry.

(II)   Seize Development Opportunities in Emerging Equipment Industry to Rapidly Strengthen
       and Improve our Business
Semiconductor Segment: The Company maintained a leading market share in IGBT module deliveries in the rail transit
and power grid sectors, ranking first domestically. Its applications in the new energy market continued to expand.
According to statistics from NE Times, the Company’s installed capacity of power modules for new energy passenger
vehicles reached 2.6076 million sets in 2025, with a market share of approximately 13.8%, ranking second only to
BYD. The shipment volume of IGBT modules in the new energy power generation market grew rapidly. In addition
to domestic business, overseas revenue increased significantly. The Yixing IGBT production line successfully reached
full production capacity, and the Zhuzhou SiC production line was put into operation smoothly. The Company made
breakthroughs in the fourth-generation trench-gate SiC MOSFET chip technology. Furthermore, the sensor business in
new energy sector stabilised and trended upwards, with a substantial increase in delivery volume.


Automotive Segment: Sales of electric drive systems for new energy passenger vehicles continued to rise throughout
the year. According to NE Times statistics, the Company’s installed volume of stators for new energy vehicle electric
drive systems reached 571,500 units in 2025, ranking 9th. The installed volume of electronic control units reached
689,100 units, ranking 6th. The Company secured designated projects for 40 new models. Its first overseas project,
the Indonesia base, was completed and put into operation. The Company also completed the development of its
5th-generation high-voltage SiC all-in-one electric drive product platform for battery electric vehicles.


New Energy Segment: The Company launched its new-generation 2000V/400kW+ string PV inverter “Chixiao”
and a new-generation energy storage converter “Yunshu” with a single unit capacity of 3.45MW. Its PV inverter
business won approximately 18GW of domestic bids, ranking among the industry leaders. New orders for wind power
converters and energy storage converters grew substantially. The Company maintained a leading domestic market
share in IGBT-based hydrogen generation power supplies.


Marine Segment: Marine equipment business leveraged synergies across three regional markets, leading to record
highs both in revenue and orders. The world’s first underwater heavy-duty electric ROV was commercially delivered,
and the largest domestically manufactured shaft-driven frequency converter in the world was installed and applied on
vessels.


Industrial Segment: The Company won bulk orders for mining truck electric drive system, consolidating our market
position; ensured continuous delivery of central air conditioner converters and medium-voltage rolling mill drive
systems, steadily enhancing our position in the industry.


Looking ahead, we will fully leverage our industrial strengths, continuously strengthen our core competitiveness, and
consolidate and enhance our standing in the industry. Concurrently, we will accelerate innovation-driven development
and business optimisation, strive to achieve high-quality and sustainable growth, and deliver greater value for all
shareholders.

    As a leading traction converter system supplier in China’s rail transit industry, the Company provides traction converter

    The Company has continued to lead the domestic rail transit electrical system market in the independent R&D and

    the establishment of a new development pattern, the Company has firmly seized the historic development
    opportunities brought by the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation, and
    advanced the development of strategic emerging industries in depth. It has become a leading domestic enterprise in

3.    Highly reliable quality and service advantages
The Company always regards product quality as the foundation of survival. To comply with the changing management
requirements of the international railway market and continuously improve the management ability and level of
its quality system, the Company has passed a series of international quality management system certifications
including ISO9001, EN15085 CL1, ISO22163, and IATF16949 certifications, has obtained CRCC certification for
relevant railway products, and conducts quality control of products in the production process. In addition, the
Company has established a life-cycle quality management and assurance system covering design, development,
procurement, manufacturing, marketing and services. Specifically, the Company identifies improvement opportunities
through process review, process inspection, internal and external audit, regular management review, irregular
quality inspection, data analysis and process improvement, and assigns relevant responsibilities to ensure that the
improvement goals are achieved. The well-established quality management system and the whole life cycle quality
management model ensure the high reliability and efficiency of products. The Company was awarded the title of
Industrial Enterprise Quality Benchmarking Enterprise by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology in 2013,
and won the second China Quality Award in 2016. The Company always upholds the quality concept of “quality-driven
Times Electric”, implements rigorous quality and safety control measures, and has built a company-wide quality
culture emphasizing that “quality is the lifeline and the supreme responsibility and honor of the Company”.


In maintenance service, the Company established the “Greenshade Service (綠蔭服務)” brand in 2004 and registered
the only “Greenshade (綠蔭)” after-sales service trademark for after-sale service in the domestic rail transit
industry. Upholding the tenet of “fast, effective and satisfactory services”, the Company provides customers with
around-the-clock, one-stop quality onsite service and continues to create value for customers. In addition, in line
with strategic maintenance planning of State Railway Group and in an ongoing effort to expand and optimise its
maintenance coverage, the Company has established maintenance branches in Qingdao and Luoyang, as well as a
number of local maintenance bases across the country.


4.    Synergy across the whole industry chain
Based on “Two Rails” and centering on “technology” and “market”, the Company has built presence in diverse
industries and formed a complete industry chain comprising “components + system + complete machine”. The
Company’s main products include rail transit electrical equipment (primarily traction converter systems of rail transit
vehicles), railway engineering machinery, communication signal systems, power semiconductors, etc. In addition,
leveraging its technologies, channels, brands and other advantageous resources in the field of rail transit equipment,
the Company actively expands to industries other than rail transit, and comprehensively improves product strength
through ongoing lean production, intensified process control, supplier management, etc. The complete industry chain
structure and the growing emerging equipment business not only bring the Company profit growth drivers, but also
serve as an important guarantee for the Company to master the whole industry chain resources and build a supplier
system with self-developed core technologies and effective cost control.

(III)   Core Technologies and R&D Progress
1.      Core technologies and their advancedness and changes during the reporting period
Since its establishment, the Company has been deeply engaged in the field of traction converter systems of rail transit
vehicles, thus developing outstanding scientific and technological innovation strength. On this basis, the Company
follows the strategy of “concentric diversification” to extend to related fields. Through independent research and
development, the Company has developed a range of core technologies including electrical system technology,
converter and control technology, industrial converter technology, train control and diagnosis technology, railway
engineering machinery technology, power semiconductor technology, communication signal technology, data and
intelligent application technology, traction power supply technology, inspection and testing technology, deep-sea
robotic technology, new energy vehicle electric drive system technology, and sensor technology. As at 31 December
2025, the Company had 3,858 valid domestic and foreign registered patents to protect its core technologies.
Moreover, it has signed confidentiality agreements and non-competition agreements with the relevant personnel to
ensure that the core technologies are not disclosed.

2.    R&D achievements during the reporting period
During the reporting period, the Company adhered to the key note of high-quality development to foster new quality
productive forces according to local conditions, strengthen the leading role of technological innovation, promote
industrial innovation through technological innovation, and achieved fruitful results in scientific and technological
innovation.


In 2025, in the rail transit business segment, the Company built a full-working-condition and high-fault-tolerance
system for the permanent magnet traction system, realizing the transformation of permanent magnet fault
response from passive handling to active management and control. It completed the prototype development of
the DC3000/750V traction and auxiliary system platform for the overseas market, with a 25% reduction in weight
and 20% reduction in volume, promoting the platformisation of overseas products. It completed the iteration of
key technologies such as the PCU and permanent magnet safety of the CR450 EMU, where the product’s technical
performance and quality are superior to those of competitors, and the train achieved over 360,000 kilometers of
stable operation assessment on the main line. It completed the iterative optimization and test verification of the
urban rail traction system based on independently customized three-level devices, realising a 20% reduction in
weight. It completed the on-board test of the Fuxing-type high-power permanent magnet freight electric locomotive,
boosting the leap of heavy-haul electric locomotives from “Hexie” series to “Fuxing” series. It achieved the
batch delivery of the fully independent system for FXD1BA on the Daqin Railway, carried out tests on 20,000-ton
combined trains, and realized the full coverage of the Company’s core products in heavy-haul railways. More than
200 locomotive automatic driving systems were installed in batches, with a cumulative operating mileage of over
8.5 million kilometers; the operation assessment was completed on the national railway Haoji Railway, with an
operation assessment mileage of over 200,000 kilometers. It broke through the ETCS multi-system integration and
switching technology, reaching the international benchmark level. Changsha Line 2 achieved the first case of CBTC
to CBTC modification in the industry, and Ningbo Line 8 FAO was fully functionally put into operation with a number
of advanced technologies. The speed-up railway train control system (LKJ upgrade) was quickly finalized, and the
vehicle-ground integrated integration technology became the industry benchmark. It completed the development
of the same-phase power supply device and energy dispatching device for Chongqing Line 15; it completed the
demonstration application of the first domestic “grid-source-storage-vehicle” collaborative function system project
for heavy-haul railways. It realized the batch promotion and application of the urban rail active power supply system.
It launched 6 types of electric transmission platforms for construction equipment adapted to complex working
conditions such as plateaus, alpine regions, and tunnel geothermal heat in a systematic manner for the first time. It
mastered key technologies such as grinding dust cleaning, air-electric hybrid braking, and dual-source hybrid drive,
and the independently developed grinding and catenary maintenance equipment successfully passed the national
railway plan review. It completed the development of the TQME6 door control platform, the first domestic platform
meeting the highest SIL4 safety level.




                                               2025 Annual Report      ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD.             43
    Report of the Directors
    In the emerging equipment business segment, the Company broke through the fourth-generation trench-gate SiC
    MOSFET chip technology, with a specific on-resistance of ≤ 2 milliohm·cm², reaching the international leading level. It
    mastered the platinum FRD chip technology, achieving a 50% reduction in leakage current and a 15% improvement
    in RRSOA, reaching the international advanced level. It broke through the 1μm Pitch ultra-fine trench IGBT
    technology, realizing a 7% improvement in current output capacity and continuously expanding its leading advantage.
    It deeply optimized and reconstructed the fluxgate signal processing algorithm and temperature drift compensation
    model, significantly improving the measurement accuracy and long-term stability of sensors under complex working
    conditions. The industrial-grade Hall ASIC chip independently designed and developed completed its first tape-out;
    the fully independently packaged 100A-level chip-level current sensor successfully rolled off the production line. It
    launched the 400kW+ photovoltaic inverter “Chixiao” and the 3.XMW energy storage PCS “Yunshu”. The string
    photovoltaic inverter developed an MPPT adaptive optimization and dynamic power distribution strategy, achieving
    5‰ control accuracy and zero overshoot in primary frequency modulation, with leading performance indicators
    in the industry. It launched the IGBT hydrogen production power supply HPS2.0 platform, with a power density
    increase of more than 40% and leading performance indicators in the industry. It completed the development of
    the fifth-generation product, where the power density of the pure electric high-voltage SiC multi-in-one assembly
    reached 4.42kW/kg, the CLTC working condition efficiency reached 93.52%, passed the third-party “high-quality
    electric drive” certification, and its technical indicators reached the industry leading level. Compared with products of
    the same power level, the 200kW hybrid five-in-one assembly is 10% lighter, reaching the industry advanced level. It
    completed the serialized development of 0.5∼4.3MW shaft generator frequency converters, realized the installation
    and application of the world’s largest localized shaft generator frequency converter on ships, and is in the industry
    leading level. It assisted in the installation and operation of the world’s first WK55 electric shovel permanent magnet
    direct drive electronic control system. The world’s first underwater heavy-duty operation electric ROV completed
    commercial delivery, with an energy efficiency improvement of 27%, leading the global trend of electrification in
    deep-sea operations. The domestic largest horsepower 1,500-meter ROV system successfully passed sea trials and was
    delivered.


    Focusing on the Company’s core technologies and main products, the Company adheres to and actively plans the
    intellectual property layout work, and continuously enhances its influence in the industry. In 2025, it added 404
    authorised patents at home and abroad, including 15 authorised overseas patents. Currently, the Company has 3,858
    authorised and valid patents, of which invention patents account for more than 60%; it presided over or participated
    in the release of 21 international, national, industrial and group standards in the fields of transportation and energy,
    continuously consolidating and improving its industry status.

IV.     RISK FACTORS
(I)     Risk of Making No Profits Yet
□Applicable    ✔ Not applicable


(II)    Risk of a Sharp Decline or Loss in Earnings
□Applicable    ✔ Not applicable


(III)   Core Competitiveness Risk
✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


As a core supplier of rail transit equipment, the Company has achieved rapid development in the new energy industry
in recent years and is quickly moving toward the leading position. In accordance with market demand and industry
technology development trends, the Company has continuously carried out research and development of new
technologies and new products, and invested a large amount of manpower, financial resources and resources. Due
to the uncertainty inherent in technology research and development, if the Company makes incorrect judgments
on the development direction of new technologies or lags behind in product research and development, it may lead
to failures in the research and development of new technologies and new products, or new products launched on
the market failing to achieve the expected benefits, which will affect the Company’s operating performance and
competitiveness.


Countermeasures: The Company will strengthen forward-looking technology research and patent barriers, keep
abreast of domestic and international technological development trends in the industry, hold regular technical
seminars, grasp the market development direction and make advance layout; meanwhile, the Company will
strengthen the linkage between scientific research and the market, accelerate product upgrading to seize the
market; furthermore, the Company will leverage advantageous industrial resources, enhance external scientific and
technological cooperation, accelerate the R&D of independent core technologies and improve the comprehensive
competitiveness of products.




                                              2025 Annual Report     ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD.            61
    Report of the Directors
    (IV)   Operating Risk
    ✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


    Demand in the rail transit industry is influenced by the macroeconomy, local fiscal strength, infrastructure investment
    pace, and government policies. Investment in urban rail and railway projects may slow down amid mounting
    local fiscal pressure, leading to risks that new order volume and delivery progress fall short of expectations, thus
    constraining growth in the Company’s traditional core business. While the emerging equipment sector is expanding
    rapidly, domestic competitors have adopted low-price competition strategies to seize market share quickly, squeezing
    profit margins and undermining the Company’s profitability through price wars.


    Countermeasures: The Company will establish regular government-enterprise communication channels and
    mechanisms to timely collect and obtain national and local policy information, organize periodic seminars to analyze
    and forecast the direction and impact of external policies, and formulate response strategies in advance; secondly,
    it will build high-level technical R&D and production platforms, strengthen the market competitiveness of existing
    products, continuously optimize and expand the product portfolio, and lead market demand.


    (V)    Financial Risk
    ✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


    As the Company accelerates the implementation of its international operation strategy, greater attention will be paid
    to the financial risks of overseas business, such as risks arising from exchange rate fluctuations, accounts receivable,
    and operating cost control. Overseas business involves settlement in multiple currencies, and sharp exchange rate
    fluctuations of project currencies will directly erode project profits and result in exchange losses. Meanwhile, overseas
    projects have long implementation cycles and large upfront investments, and customers in different countries vary
    significantly in credit standing, which poses risks of payment arrears and even bad debts. Furthermore, overseas
    projects face fierce international competition, and uncontrollable factors such as geopolitical conflicts and operational
    sanctions may directly lead to project suspension, asset losses, and considerable operational uncertainty.


    Countermeasures: The Company shall conduct risk assessment and analysis on overseas projects, enhance the
    risk prevention awareness of relevant personnel, and continuously monitor the trend of exchange rate fluctuations;
    establish a full-process exchange rate risk management mechanism, formulate appropriate foreign exchange risk
    management plans and organize their implementation; adopt foreign exchange risk management plans at the early
    stage of conducting foreign currency business to lock in foreign exchange risks. For signed foreign currency contracts,
    the Company shall adopt forward exchange settlement and use RMB for settlement as much as possible.




62 ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD. 2025 Annual Report
                                                     Report of the Directors
(VI)   Industry Risk
✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


The new energy vehicle industry is currently in an extremely competitive environment. Affected by the concentrated
outbreak of structural contradictions arising from the rapid industrial expansion, internal competition within the
industry has become particularly severe. In the short term, automakers are blindly pursuing scale at the expense of
profits, making it difficult for both upstream and downstream industrial chains to achieve profitability. Competition in
the electric drive industry has intensified, posing significant challenges to the Company’s profitability.


Countermeasures: The Company will actively collect national policies and industry information, strengthen
research on market trends and business strategies, establish a market risk early-warning mechanism, and improve
market operation strategies; carry out platform-based low-cost design to quickly achieve price optimization for
mass-produced products; implement cost-oriented refined procurement category management, optimize the supply
chain, and enhance product engineering and mass low-cost manufacturing capabilities.


(VII) Macro Environment Risk
✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


Global economic growth is slowing down, while geopolitical conflicts and trade barriers continue to intensify.
Domestically, the economy pursues progress while maintaining stability, with domestic demand as the core,
consumption recovering moderately, service consumption leading the way, and policy support boosting confidence;
efforts to stabilize growth and promote transformation are advancing in parallel. Overseas, risks related to the security
of overseas assets and compliance control over international operations are becoming increasingly severe. Meanwhile,
ongoing uncertainties such as climate risks and geopolitical tensions are creating significant uncertainty for the global
economic recovery.


Countermeasures: The Company will continuously track the latest domestic policies as well as relevant information
and developments in politics, economy, and industry of the countries and regions involved in its overseas business,
especially strengthen the risk management of foreign-related projects, and effectively prevent risks while expanding
overseas markets.

    2.    Revenue and cost analysis
    ✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


    During the reporting period, the Company achieved revenue of RMB28.703 billion, representing a year-on-year
    increase of 15.23% compared with RMB24.909 billion in the same period of the previous year.


    1.    Rail transit equipment segment delivers stable and stabilizing revenue
    During the reporting period, the Company achieved revenue of RMB15.806 billion from the rail transit equipment
    segment, representing a year-on-year increase of 7.99% compared with RMB14.636 billion in the same period of
    the previous year. In particular, the rail transit electrical equipment segment achieved revenue of RMB12.106 billion,
    representing a year-on-year increase of 10.15% compared with RMB10.990 billion in the same period of the previous
    year; the rail engineering machinery segment achieved revenue of RMB1.899 billion, representing a year-on-year
    increase of 0.39% compared with RMB1.891 billion in the same period of the previous year; the communication signal
    system segment achieved revenue of RMB1.149 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 4.02% compared
    with RMB1.105 billion in the same period of the previous year; and the other rail transit equipment segment achieved
    revenue of RMB0.652 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 0.26% compared with RMB0.650 billion in the
    same period of the previous year.


    2.    The emerging equipment segment poised for a breakthrough
    During the reporting period, the Company achieved revenue of RMB12.780 billion from the emerging equipment
    segment, representing a year-on-year increase of 26.35% compared with RMB10.115 billion in the same period of
    the previous year. In particular, the semiconductor segment achieved revenue of RMB5.360 billion, representing
    a year-on-year increase of 30.43% compared with RMB4.110 billion in the same period of the previous year;
    the automotive segment achieved revenue of RMB3.268 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 27.22%
    compared with RMB2.569 billion in the same period of the previous year; the new energy segment achieved revenue
    of RMB2.401 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 17.93% compared with RMB2.036 billion in the same
    period of the previous year; the marine segment achieved revenue of RMB1.030 billion, representing a year-on-year
    increase of 19.11% compared with RMB0.865 billion in the same period of the previous year; and the industrial
    segment achieved revenue of RMB0.721 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 34.61% compared with
    RMB0.535 billion in the same period of the previous year.

    Description of production and sales volume


    The traction converter systems of rail transit vehicles produced by the Company need to be customised based on
    customer needs, and the core of the system includes software and system integrated modules and involves many
    types of hardware and devices. Some non-critical hardware may be obtained through purchase. Accordingly, the
    traditional concept of production capacity is not applicable to such product.


    The production and sales volume of the Company’s power semiconductor devices (device products) and railway
    engineering machinery (complete machines) are set out in the table above. Among them, the sales volume of power
    semiconductor devices includes the volume of sales to companies included in the Company’s consolidated scope.


    In 2025, the Company’s production and sales volume of rail engineering machinery and vehicles decreased slightly,
    with the decline concentrated in overhaul and urban rail production lines, mainly due to the reduction in the overhaul
    plans approved by railway bureaus and the overall weaker market demand for urban rail transit in 2025.

Risk analysis and description of           1.    Risk analysis of the Company’s foreign exchange derivatives trading business
  control measures for derivatives
  positions during the reporting           (1)   Market risk
  period (including but not limited              Foreign exchange rates may fluctuate significantly due to changes in domestic and overseas economic situation,
  to market risk, liquidity risk, credit         exposing the Company’s foreign exchange derivatives trading to certain market risks. In reviewing foreign exchange
  risk, operational risk, legal risk,            derivatives trading business and annual plan, the Company strictly adheres to the principle of hedging and the
  etc.)                                          purpose of reducing risk exposure of its principal operations, selects derivative products with simple structure,
                                                 manageable risks and strong liquidity, and matches the business structure with its principal operations in terms of
                                                 variety, size, direction, term and other elements of exposure positions to ensure the hedging relationship between its
                                                 derivatives business and the hedged underlyers. Speculative trading is prohibited to effectively guard against market
                                                 risks.

                                           (2)   Operational risk
                                                 Foreign exchange derivatives business is highly professional and complex, and certain risks may be caused by
                                                 operators who fail to understand derivatives information in time or at all, or fail to execute transactions in
                                                 accordance with rules and policies. The Company will continuously improve its foreign exchange risk management
                                                 system, clearly separate front, middle and back offices for derivatives business, ensure that operators have relevant
                                                 experience or business qualifications, and strictly prevent operational risks through employee audits, systematic
                                                 controls and hierarchical authorisation and approval mechanisms.

                                           (3)   Liquidity Risk
                                                 Unreasonable purchase arrangement of foreign exchange derivatives may trigger liquidity risk of the Company’s
                                                 funds. The foreign exchange derivatives are based on the Company’s foreign exchange assets and liabilities and
                                                 match with the actual foreign exchange income and expenditure, and the Company selects appropriate foreign
                                                 exchange derivatives in a timely manner and appropriately chooses net settlement foreign exchange derivatives,
                                                 which can ensure that there are sufficient funds for settlement at the time of delivery, so as to reduce liquidity risk.

                                           (4)   Performance risk
                                                 If the counterparty of foreign exchange derivatives fails to execute contract at the agreed price upon expiry, the
                                                 corresponding foreign exchange exposure would not be closed, leading to a failure in managing exchange rate risk
                                                 as expected. The counterparties of foreign exchange derivatives transactions of the Company are all large commercial
                                                 banks with high credit ratings and long-term business relationship with the Company, so as to avoid performance
                                                 risk.

    Report of the Directors
                                            2.        Risk prevention and control measures adopted by the Company for foreign exchange derivatives trading business

                                            (1)       All foreign exchange derivatives trading varieties carried out by the Company are those with simple structure,
                                                      manageable risks and strong liquidity that are closely related to the basic business, and such foreign exchange
                                                      derivatives match the basic business in terms of variety, size, direction, term, etc., so as to follow the Company’s
                                                      prudent and robust risk management principle, avoid speculative transactions and effectively guard against market
                                                      risks.

                                                      Manual for Financial Derivatives Business, which clearly stipulate the operating principles, approval authority,
                                                      department setting and staffing, internal operation process, internal risk reporting system and risk handling
                                                      procedures, information disclosure and information isolation measures of foreign exchange derivatives transactions
                                                      to avoid operational risk.

                                            (3)       The Company will carefully select counterparties for foreign exchange derivatives trading, requiring them to be large
                                                      commercial banks with high credit ratings and long-term business relationship with the Company, strictly review
                                                      the terms of contracts entered into with qualified financial institutions and strictly implement the risk management
                                                      system to effectively avoid performance risk.

VI.    DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS ON THE FUTURE DEVELOPMENT OF THE
       COMPANY
(I)    Industry Landscape and Trends
✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


As an important component of the modern transportation system and a major livelihood project, railways have made
significant contributions to boosting economic recovery and facilitating public travel. According to authoritative
documents including the Outline of the Strategic Plan for Railway Pioneering in Building a Transport Power in the
New Era and the national railway development plans, the national railway operating mileage is expected to reach
approximately 180,000 kilometers by the end of 2030. Among them, high-speed railways will increase from 50,000
kilometers to 60,000 kilometers, with growth rates lower than those during the 14th Five-Year Plan period. By
the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, China’s railway infrastructure network had become relatively complete.
The national development focus has gradually shifted from large-scale construction to “strengthening weak areas,
enhancing integration, and improving quality and efficiency”, namely the optimization, operation and maintenance,
and intelligent upgrading of the existing network. Meanwhile, approvals for new railway projects by the National
Development and Reform Commission and other authorities have been tightened, resulting in a notable slowdown
in railway investment growth. The entire market is shifting from “competition for incremental expansion” to
“competition for existing stock”. Against the deeper implementation of the regional coordinated development
strategy, as well as national strategies including the “new infrastructure” initiative, accelerated networking of urban
rail transit in city clusters and metropolitan areas, and faster development of suburban (metro-area) railways, intercity
railways and suburban (metro-area) railways will embrace growth. With the expanding stock of rail transit equipment
and the continuous entry of equipment into the maintenance cycle, the inspection, repair and maintenance market is
expected to grow further. The rail transit industry is an important pillar for national economic development and safe
operation. In terms of the domestic market competition landscape, Beijing Zongheng Electromechanical Technology
Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Academy of Railway Sciences, maintains strong competitiveness in the EMU traction
converter system market thanks to its rich experience in product R&D, manufacturing and on-board operation. It
has achieved full coverage in the railway industry and continuously strengthened its market development efforts. In
addition, subsidiaries of CRRC Corporation Limited, including CRRC Qingdao Sifang Rolling Stock Research Institute
Co., Ltd., CRRC Yongji Motor Co., Ltd., CRRC Dalian Locomotive Research Institute Co., Ltd., and CRRC Dalian
Electric Traction R&D Center Co., Ltd., are also engaged in businesses related to rail transit traction converter systems,
which places them in partial competition with the Company. In the overseas market competition landscape, developed
markets have long been dominated by leading international enterprises such as Siemens AG, Alstom SA, and
Bombardier Inc., which have formed a relatively mature industrial ecosystem in terms of technological accumulation,
brand influence and market layout. Against this background, relevant Chinese enterprises have continued to advance
their internationalization strategies and actively explore overseas markets, while continuously addressing systematic
challenges including technical standards, market access, and local integration.




                                                2025 Annual Report       ZHUZHOU CRRC TIMES ELECTRIC CO., LTD.               83
    Report of the Directors
    The overall trend of urban rail transit construction has slowed down, with local governments facing high debt ratios
    and significantly tightened fiscal policies, and urban rail transit has shifted from rapid construction to a stage of
    high-quality operation. At the same time, against the background of the national strategy of carbon peaking and
    carbon neutrality, the China Urban Rail Transit Association has successively issued four documents during the “14th
    Five-Year Plan” period, namely the “Outline for the Development of Smart Urban Rail Transit in China”, the “Action
    Plan for Green Urban Rail Transit in China”, the “Guidelines for the Integrated Development of Urban Rail Transit in
    China” and the “Development Plan for Domestic Innovation-Driven Urban Rail Transit in China”, which have pointed
    out the direction for the development of the urban rail transit industry and outlined a comprehensive, systematic and
    highly forward-looking development blueprint. These four documents are closely linked and complementary to each
    other: the standard system of smart urban rail transit provides a basis for green evaluation, integrated coordination
    and domestic innovation verification; the energy-saving indicators of green urban rail transit force the optimization
    of smart technologies and domestic innovation breakthroughs; cases of integrated urban rail transit feed back the
    technological iteration of smart, green and domestic innovation; the achievements of domestic innovation-driven
    urban rail transit support the large-scale implementation of smart, green and integrated development. With smart
    efficiency improvement, green carbon reduction, integrated value-added and domestic innovation as the foundation,
    the four aspects of “smart, green, integrated and innovative” together form a new strategic system of “led by
    independent innovation and multi-dimensional coordinated development” for China’s urban rail transit. In terms of
    the competitive landscape, relying on in-depth cooperation with owners in some regions, Jiangsu Jingwei Rail Transit
    Equipment Co., Ltd. obtained traction systems for more than 600 metro vehicles in Jinan, Xiamen, Nanjing and
    other places in 2025, maintaining strong market competitiveness, and Xinyu Bombardier Traction Systems Co., Ltd.
    obtained traction systems for nearly 200 metro vehicles in Shijiazhuang, performing actively in market competition.


    Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality is an extensive and profound systemic economic and social
    transformation. With the in-depth advancement of the national “dual carbon” strategy, a hundreds-of-billions-level
    new energy market with great growth potential has been fostered. Emerging industries highly aligned with the
    national “dual carbon strategy”, such as wind-solar-storage-hydrogen equipment, photovoltaic projects, automotive
    electric drive systems, power semiconductors and sensors, are currently developing rapidly, also providing enterprises
    with broad market space. In terms of the competitive landscape, the oligopoly effect in the photovoltaic inverter
    market continued in 2025, and Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd., Huawei Digital Energy Technology Co., Ltd., CRRC
    Times Electric Co., Ltd., Tebian Electric Apparatus Stock Co., Ltd. and Sineng Electric Co., Ltd. still remained in
    the first echelon. In the wind power converter market, leading enterprises in the industry such as Sungrow Power
    Supply Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Hopewind Electric Co., Ltd. and Xinjiang Goldwind Science & Technology Co., Ltd. still
    occupied important market shares. According to NE Times statistics, in 2025, Fudi Power Co., Ltd.’s electric drive
    system installed capacity retained the first place with a 19.1% share, relying on the continuous strong sales of BYD
    Dynasty and Ocean Network models to provide a solid foundation; Huawei Digital Energy Technology Co., Ltd. ranked
    second with 809,500 units and an 8.2% share; Tesla Inc.’s slight increase of 1.1% also reflects that the optimization
    of its local supply chain has entered a stable period, and the top three enterprises accounted for more than 35% of
    the market share. In the power semiconductor market, Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics Co., Ltd. gave play to the
    advantages of the IDM model, with core chip production lines operating at full capacity and SiC production lines
    gradually ramping up; in addition, international leading enterprises represented by Infineon Technologies AG have
    maintained long-term technological and market leadership through long-term accumulation. In the sensor market,
    LEM S.A. ranked first in the global power sensor market; in addition, domestic player Anhui Sinomags Technology
    Co., Ltd. has developed rapidly in the magnetic sensor market in recent years, becoming another major competitor of
    the Company, and officially submitted an application for listing in 2025.

(II)   Development Strategy of the Company
✔ Applicable   □Not applicable


The Company will fully align with national strategies, fully recognize its responsibilities and missions, focus on its core
businesses, fully leverage the advantages of coordinated development of its six industrial sectors, and further achieve
high-quality development. Under the guidance of the development vision of “Building a Green and Smart New Era
through Technological Innovation”, the Company has established the “1246” strategic framework:


Anchor the first-class positioning and adhere to one main line. With the goal of building a world-class enterprise,
we will become a world-class electrical system solution provider in the transportation and energy sectors; take
high-quality development as the main line, and drive the continuous improvement of profitability through the
improvement of management capabilities, optimization of industrial structure, and iteration of technologies and
products.


Focus on two approaches and fulfill dual responsibilities. We will actively serve national major strategies through
two approaches: continuously improving core competitiveness and enhancing core functions. Internally, we will
cultivate the two core competitiveness of converter and control technologies to shape sustainable efficiency-creating
competitive advantages; externally, we will assume the mission of “serving the country’s major interests” to achieve
the resonance between national strategic missions and corporate value creation.


Adhere to the “Four Higher Standards” and create outstanding value. Through high-quality and efficient operation,
we will build a CRRC with “Four Higher Standards” that enjoys higher social respect, higher shareholder recognition,
higher customer satisfaction and higher employee happiness.


Develop six industrial sectors and build six core competencies. We will focus on fostering six industrial sectors
featuring balanced and tiered development: rail transit, semiconductors, automotive, new energy, marine and
industrial sectors; and strengthen the six core competencies: Party-building leadership, technological leadership,
sector-based governance, reform empowerment, digital-intelligent development, and global operations.

    Report of the Directors
    Mechanism for Protecting Non-controlling Interests
    To protect non-controlling interests, the Company has established and implemented certain governance measures,
    which include:


    (1)   In accordance with the Articles, directors who are interested in the transactions should disclose their respective
          interest, and shall not vote in respect of the transactions in which they are interested and shall not be counted
          towards the quorum of the meeting. Therefore, for the connected transactions between the Group and CRRC
          Group, Mr. Li Donglin, Mr. Shang Jing and Mr. Xu Shaolong did not vote in respect of the relevant Board
          resolutions and were not counted towards the quorum of the meetings approving the relevant resolutions due
          to conflict of interest.


    (2)   An independent professional management team of the Group responsible for negotiating and reviewing the
          terms of transactions with the suppliers and customers (including CRRC Group) has been established. The
          members of the management team include the staff of the Group with relevant technical and sales expertise,
          and the terms of duties of the management team allow it to make independent business judgments. The
          management team reports to the Board, while the Board is accountable to the Shareholders of the Company
          as a whole.


    (3)   The Company’s auditor has provided quarterly reports to the independent non-executive Directors on all
          transactions conducted between the Group and CRRC Group.


    (4)   When making purchases, the Group has endeavoured to obtain tenders or quotations from a number of
          independent suppliers, and select successful bidders (where applicable) based on objective standards such as
          the price and quality of products, delivery schedule and services.


    (5)   Subject to (1) above, all independent non-executive Directors have attended the Board meetings for deciding
          whether the Group should conduct special transactions with CRRC Group.


    (6)   The terms for the supply and purchase arrangements entered into between the Group and CRRC Group
          are subject to quarterly review by the independent non-executive Directors, and opinions regarding such
          transactions are disclosed by the Company to the Shareholders by way of announcements. Independent
          non-executive Directors may request an independent party having at least 10 years’ experience in the
          locomotive and rolling stock manufacturing industry to participate in assessing the terms of the sales and
          purchases agreements, and to provide their opinions to the independent non-executive Directors.

Non-competition and Indemnity Deeds
The Company entered into a non-competition and indemnity deed with CRRC ZELRI and CRRC Group on 30 November
2006 (the “Non-Competition and Indemnity Deed”), pursuant to which CRRC ZELRI and CRRC Group respectively
undertook not to, and procure any of its associates (as defined under the Hong Kong Listing Rules, excluding the
Group) not to carry on businesses that are in competition with the Group’s businesses. In 2015, CSR merged with
CNR and formed CRRC; China Northern Locomotive & Rolling Stock Industry (Group) Corporation merged with CSR
Group and formed CRRC Group. As certain businesses of the subsidiaries of CNR overlap with those of the Group,
there are certain business overlaps between CRRC Group and the Group. Accordingly, CRRC issued an undertaking
letter regarding the avoidance of competition with the Company (the “Undertaking Letter”) to the Company on 5
August 2015, in which it provided non-competition undertakings as follows:


•     CRRC will grant the Company a call option, pursuant to which, the Company will be entitled to elect, at its
      own discretion, when to request CRRC to sell the competing businesses of CRRC to the Company;


•     CRRC further granted the Company a pre-emptive right, pursuant to which, if CRRC proposes to sell the
      competing business to an independent third party, CRRC shall offer to the Company the competing business
      first on the same conditions, and the sale to the third party may only be effected after the Company declined
      to purchase the competing business;


•     the decision of the Company to exercise the aforesaid option and the pre-emptive right to purchase shall be
      made by the independent non-executive Directors of the Company;


•     the exercise of the aforesaid option and the pre-emptive right to purchase will be subject to the applicable
      regulatory and disclosure requirements and Shareholders’ approval at the general meeting in the places of
      listing of CRRC and the Company respectively;


•     the aforesaid non-competition undertaking will be effective from the date of issuance to the time when the
      Company is de-listed or CRRC ceases to be an indirect controlling Shareholder of the Company.
